description: Increases an existing video's resolution (2x, 3x or 4x) and returns the new job's id immediately. It does NOT wait for the result and does not change the content: same shot, more pixels. WHEN: the user asks to upscale, enhance, sharpen or increase the resolution of a video they already have. It is not how you make a video look different (that is a new generation). THE CARD: this call already opened the aicut card: do not call `show_generation` for this job. WAIT: `wait_for_generation` (this id, `media`), again at once while `terminal: false`, then one short line; no `get_*` polling, timers, background shells or narrating the wait. No card? Give the user the `url`. COST: this spends the user's tokens; the price depends on the clip's LENGTH and the resolution it lands in, so a long clip or a big factor costs many times a short one. The clip's length is MEASURED BY THE SERVER: that measurement is the price. A clip it cannot measure (a WebM, an unreadable header) is REFUSED uncharged: re-encode to MP4. An external url costs one media-ingest slot: quote and create from the SAME url to pay it once. SPENDS TOKENS: price with `estimate_only: true`, ask in the SAME message as the price, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase (SPENDING RULES, this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: a reused `idempotency_key` REPLAYS the first job whatever the settings: never reuse one for a new generation (this server's instructions).

source_video.description: URL of the video to upscale. A URL from this account's generations or uploads, or a public https URL (imported first); another account's is refused.

upscale_factor.description: Times larger: 1, 2, 3 or 4 (default 2). A result over 7680px on either side is refused before anything is charged. Only if the user asked; never to save tokens, never carried over.
